# Plass

> Plass is a React UI component library published to npm as `plass-ui`. Behaviour and accessibility come from [Base UI](https://base-ui.com) primitives; styling comes from [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com) v4. It ships as ESM only with type declarations included, has one runtime dependency (`@base-ui/react`), and supports dark mode out of the box.

The design language: **a Plass surface is a key of tinted glass resting on a clear sheet.** Every surface answers one question — is this pressed, or does it hold something? A thing that is pressed is tinted glass: a two-stop gradient at 135° whose ends are the two ends of a colour family at one lightness (indigo to azure, vermilion to rose), a drop shadow **tinted with that family**, and a bloom of light that follows the pointer. There is deliberately no specular highlight and no inset edge on a filled control — a gradient that turns carries the form, and a highlight over the top of it reads as lacquer. A thing that holds something is clear glass: translucent, `blur(22px) saturate(160%)`, a white hairline round it, and never dyed. A control never moves — there is no `transform` on press — it answers in light and depth: `brightness(1.05)` on hover and `brightness(0.95)` on press, with the elevation going one step up and one step down.

`elevation` defaults to **1 on a PlButton and 0 on a PlTextField**: a key rests on the sheet, a field is cut into it.

Every component draws from one shared prop vocabulary, so `size="md"` means the same thing everywhere:

```ts
type PlassSize = 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl';
type PlassColor = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info';
type PlassDensity = 'default' | 'compact';
type PlassVariant = 'solid' | 'glass' | 'ghost';
type PlassElevation = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3;
```

`color` is one of six semantic families, never an arbitrary value like `#3558ef`. Setup is `npm install plass-ui`, then one line in the app's CSS entry point — `@import 'plass-ui/styles.css';`. That file ships compiled, so Tailwind is not a requirement on the consumer's side. A project that already runs Tailwind v4 imports `plass-ui/tailwind.css` instead, which is the token sheet and registers the package as a Tailwind source, so consumers never write an `@source` of their own.

**Version 0.0.1 is a preview.** Every component is exported under a `Pl` prefix — `PlButton`, `PlTextField`, `PlAccordion` — because the bare names are the most-taken identifiers in the ecosystem, and because the design language is meant to be portable to other toolkits. The shared prop vocabulary keeps the `Plass` prefix (`PlassSize`), and so do the CSS tokens (`--plass-*`).

Documentation is available in English (served from `/`) and Korean (served from `/ko/`). The links below are the English pages; prefix any path with `/ko` for the Korean version.

## Guide

- [Getting started](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/guide/getting-started): Install, the one-line CSS setup, what the bundled reset does, the Tailwind path, the page wash the glass needs under it, first component, dark mode via `data-theme` or a class, browser support.
- [Design language](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/design/design-language): The tinted-glass rule and everything that follows from it — the three layers of a filled surface, why the gradient turns instead of shading, the three-strength glass ladder, the one inset shadow, tinted shadows, brightness-based press, the pointer-following interaction light, the size and radius ladders, and the implementation rules.
- [Colour](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/design/color): The six semantic families as gradient sweeps, the three hand-picked tokens per family, why a family's colour does not change with the theme, the measured contrast table (every stop within 0.15 of 4.5:1), and how to override a family.
- [Prop conventions](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/design/prop-conventions): What the shared props mean, the naming rules a new component is checked against, and the three state props with their focus and native-attribute behaviour.

## Components

- [All components](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/): Every released component on one page, each card a running preview rather than a picture.

### Display

- [PlTable](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/display/table): A grid of data on a glass sheet. Takes `columns` and `rows` rather than markup, so the headings and the cells cannot drift apart; a column carries `key`, `header`, `width`, `align` and an optional `render`. `striped`, `hoverable`, `stickyHeader`, `caption`, `empty` and `onRowClick`. A clickable row keeps its `<tr>` semantics and gains a tab stop rather than a `role="button"`. Cell padding and alignment are inline styles, because host stylesheets style `td`/`th` by tag name at a specificity a utility class cannot outrank. It is generic in `Row` and so takes no `ref`.
- [PlHotKeys](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/display/hot-keys): A keyboard key, a combination of them, or the four movement keys as an inverted-T `cluster`. `Mod` is the token the rest exist for — the only one whose *meaning* changes with the platform (⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere); `os` overrides the detection for a page that must name a platform. Every glyph key carries its real name in a visually hidden box, because a screen reader announces `⌘` as "place of interest sign". The platform is resolved through `useSyncExternalStore` so a server-rendered page hydrates without a mismatch. `PlKbd` is exported as one cap. It displays a shortcut; it does not bind one.
- [PlTextLink](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/display/text-link): A link, in a sentence or on its own. No surface, no height, and — like nothing else in the library — **no default `color` and no default `size`**, because a link in a paragraph is the paragraph's colour with a line under it. `underline` is `'always' | 'hover' | 'none'` rather than a boolean. `newTab` sets `target`, merges `noopener noreferrer` into any `rel` the caller wrote, draws the external arrow and adds a visually hidden line for a screen reader. The component's class is doubled in CSS (`.plass-link.plass-link`) so a host page's `.prose a` cannot outrank it.

### Feedback

- [PlAlert](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/feedback/alert): A message about something that happened, set into the page it is about. An alert *is* the coloured thing, so its sheet takes the tint (unlike every container). `color` defaults to `info`, not `primary` — an alert is a note, not the primary anything. Each family draws its own shape as well as its own colour, so the severity does not depend on colour alone. `warning` and `danger` get `role="alert"`, the rest `role="status"`. The three shapes — bare line, line with glyph, headline plus detail — are one component with different slots filled. `onClose` is what makes the dismiss button appear; the component never hides itself.
- [PlModal](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/feedback/modal): A sheet that takes the page away until it is answered, built on Base UI's Dialog — focus trap, scroll lock, aria wiring and focus restoration are all the primitive's. No `variant` and no `elevation`: a modal has already taken the page, and one that could be told to sit flat would be one that could be told to stop being a modal. `title` becomes the `<h2>`, `description` the accessible description, `actions` the end-aligned bottom row; `PlModalClose` is exported so an uncontrolled modal's Cancel button needs no state. The sheet caps its own height and scrolls only its body. Opening animates opacity alone.

### Inputs

- [PlButton](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/button): A control that runs an action. `variant` `size` `color` `density` `elevation`, plus `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `loading`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `fullWidth` and `render`. `elevation` defaults to 1; `solid` is a pane of tinted glass whose gradient turns in hue, `glass` wears the family in its label, `ghost` has no surface until hovered. Every variant carries `.plass-glow`, a bloom that follows the pointer and flashes on press.
- [PlTextField](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/text-field): Single- or multi-line text input. The label, the description and the error are part of the component, wired together by Base UI's Field. `variant` defaults to `glass`; `solid` is a well cut into the sheet rather than a tinted pane, because a gradient under a caret is not legible. `error` also turns the field invalid, which re-points the whole slot family at `danger`.
- [PlCheckbox](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/checkbox): A single yes/no, built on Base UI's Checkbox. Clear glass with a hairline until ticked, then the family's gradient — the one place the library expresses a state by swapping the whole surface rather than shifting a step, because on and off are not two strengths of one material. No `variant`. The tick has its own size and radius ladders (`tickSizeClasses`, `tickRadiusClasses`), because a radius sized for a 40px control turns an 18px box into a circle. `label`/`description`/`error` from Base UI's Field; `indeterminate` gives the third state and `aria-checked="mixed"`.
- [PlFilePicker](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/file-picker): A box you drop files on, or click to open the file dialog. No Base UI primitive — a dropzone is a div listening for four drag events plus an `<input type="file">`. It gets right the two things hand-rolled dropzones miss: a drag *depth counter* (dragenter/dragleave fire per child, so a boolean flickers) and applying `accept` to drops (the browser enforces it on its own dialog only). `maxFiles` counts against what is already held. `onReject` reports every refusal with a reason — `type`, `size` or `count`. The dashed edge is the one non-solid line in the library. `formatFileSize` is exported alongside it.
- [PlPagination](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/pagination): The strip of page numbers under a long list. Every button is a real `PlButton`, so it inherits the surface, the press signature and the height ladder. `count`, `page`/`defaultPage`, `onPageChange`, `siblingCount`, `boundaryCount`, `showArrows`, `showEdges`. The slot count stays constant as the window slides, and a one-page gap is filled with the page rather than an ellipsis. `getPageHref` turns every number into a real `<a href>` a crawler can follow; a handler alongside it cancels the navigation for a client-side router. Renders a `<nav>` around a `<ul>` with `aria-current="page"` and a live-region status line.
- [PlRadioGroup](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/radio-group): A set of options where exactly one is chosen, built on Base UI's RadioGroup — the set takes one tab stop and the arrow keys move within it. `PlRadioGroup` holds the set and `PlRadio` is one option; `size`, `color` and `readOnly` are inherited from the group, because a radio says nothing on its own. The dot is round, one of only two round things in the library. `orientation` defaults to `vertical`.
- [PlSegmentedButton](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/segmented-button): Two or more choices in one pill, exactly one taken. Built on Base UI's RadioGroup — `role="radiogroup"`, one tab stop, arrow keys, `aria-checked` — because a segmented button *is* "exactly one of these"; `aria-pressed` toggles would announce four independent switches. The groove carries `--plass-well`; on `solid` the tile is the family's gradient with its tinted lift, a key riding in a groove. The tile animates `left`/`top`/`width`/`height` measured off the chosen segment rather than a `transform`, so no label is resampled while it moves, and it is not mounted until something is chosen so the first choice appears in place. `PlSegment` inherits `variant`, `size` and `density` from the set.
- [PlSelect](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/select): One value chosen from a list, built on Base UI's Select. The trigger is drawn on `PlTextField`'s shell (`fieldRestClasses` in `internal/styles.ts`), so a select and a field in the same form are the same object; `solid` is the well, not a tinted pane. Options are `items` (data, not children) because the trigger has to know the labels before the popup opens. `label`/`description`/`error` come from Base UI's Field; `error` re-points the family at `danger`. The trigger is held open at the width of its longest label so choosing a shorter option does not shrink it. The popup is portalled and its positioner carries `.plass-portal`.
- [PlSlider](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/slider): A value chosen along a range, built on Base UI's Slider. The rail is a groove carrying `--plass-well` — the same inset shadow a `solid` field is drawn with — and the filled run is the family's gradient, with the thumb ringed in `--plass-surface` so it never dissolves into it. An array `value` makes it a range slider; there is no `range` prop. No `variant`: a slider is a groove and a key at once, and neither has a choice to offer. `label`, `description`, `showValue` (a function gets Base UI's localised strings), `orientation`.
- [PlSwitch](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/inputs/switch): An immediate on/off, built on Base UI's Switch. Off, the track is the groove carrying `--plass-well`; on, it is the family's gradient with its tinted lift. The thumb keeps `--plass-surface` in both states — it is the light on the track, not a second coloured object — and it is the one thing in the library that moves. No `variant`. `labelPlacement` puts the label before the track for a settings list. Choose it over `PlCheckbox` when the change takes effect immediately; if there is a Save button underneath, it should have been a checkbox.

### Surfaces

- [PlCard](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/surfaces/card): The sheet everything else on a screen is grouped onto. `title`, `subtitle`, `headerAction`, `footer` and the body are slots rather than sub-components. `elevation` defaults to 1 — a card lies on the page wash. `dividers` scores the sheet instead of spacing its sections; `padded={false}` gives up the inset for full-bleed content; `interactive` lifts the sheet under the pointer, which is the one `transform` in the library, allowed because a card holds content rather than being pressed. It adds no role — a clickable card takes a real element through `render`.
- [PlTabs](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/surfaces/tabs): One set of panels, one of which is shown, built on Base UI's Tabs — roving focus, the arrow keys on the bar's own axis, the `tab`/`tabpanel` roles and the `aria-controls` wiring. `PlTab` and `PlTabPanel` are written as siblings and sorted apart by the component; there is no `PlTabList` to remember. `activateOnFocus` is off by default, because automatic activation fires a request per tab walked past once a panel fetches. `variant` `glass` is the classic rule-and-indicator bar; `solid` is a groove with a **clear** pane in it, deliberately not the gradient — that tile belongs to `PlSegmentedButton`. The indicator animates `left`/`top`/`width`/`height` from Base UI's `--active-tab-*`, never a transform.
- [PlAccordion](https://plass-ui.cdget.com/components/surfaces/accordion): A stack of sections that fold open one at a time, built on Base UI's Accordion. `PlAccordion` holds the stack and `PlAccordionItem` is one fold; `size`, `density` and `dividers` are inherited from the stack rather than set per item. `variant` defaults to `glass` and is read the way a container reads it — `solid` is the densest clear glass, never a tinted pane, because a sheet holds other people's content and is never dyed. `multiple` lets more than one stay open; `dividers` (on by default) scores the pane instead of tiling it. The panel animates its height from Base UI's measured `--accordion-panel-height`.
